title: Kanungum / Conungum
summary: Kanungum is a Calverton-area placename in Riverhead, also recorded as Conungum or Conungam and interpreted as a boundary enclosed place or boundary village.
introduction_content: Kanungum is the primary Tooker entry for the Calverton-area name also recorded as Conungum or Conungam. Tooker links it to a locality midway between Manorville and Riverhead, where later settlement preserved the older name.
history_content: The fuller geographic clue appears in Tooker's earlier Conungum cross-reference, where he cites Munsell for Calverton, Riverhead. The history belongs to a group of boundary-related names that Tooker also compares with Conegums and Konkhunganik.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Kanungum, Conungum, Conungam, and related boundary forms. The name is interpreted as a boundary enclosed place or boundary village, with the interpretation kept tentative because spellings and boundary language vary across the sources.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names represent a convergence of Indigenous language, history, culture, and environmental knowledge.”

— Xatśūll First Nation, Cumulative Effects Knowledge and Land Use Evaluation Study (2024), Place-name discussion, PDF page 92
land_loss_content: Kanungum preserves a boundary-focused placename in the Riverhead interior. Recording it separately from nearby boundary-name comparisons keeps the Calverton locality visible without merging it into unrelated creek or pond records.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for modern Calverton in the Riverhead area, not an exact historic village boundary or surveyed line.
